memory_candidates.content: In bash, `IFS=$'\t' read -r a b c` silently COLLAPSES consecutive tab delimiters (tab, like space and newline, is an IFS-whitespace character, not a plain field separator) -- an empty middle field between two tabs vanishes and the next field's value shifts left. Confirmed: `IFS=$'\t' read -r a b c <<< $'x\t\tz'` yields a=x b=z c=(empty), not a=x b=(empty) c=z. This silently corrupts any tab-delimited jq/@tsv + bash `read` pipeline whenever a middle field can be empty (e.g. a nullable `topic` field). Fix: use a non-whitespace IFS character (ASCII 0x1F unit separator, or comma) instead of tab -- `read` preserves an empty field for any non-whitespace-class delimiter.

When refactoring a selection/engine function to support BOTH a single composed call (preserving exact pre-refactor behavior) and several independent per-criterion calls within the same script invocation (e.g. a multi-option batch render), any invocation-scoped dedup set (like a 'reported pairs' set meant to fire at most once per whole script run) must be a script-level global, not a function-local re-declared on every call -- otherwise each independent call gets its own fresh set and the dedup silently stops working across calls. Pair this with a SEPARATE per-call local subset (populated alongside the global) when a later per-call computation (e.g. a conflict-free-subset second pass) must only see what THIS call discovered, not everything the global has accumulated across all calls so far.
